sections.html:
Grady County sits on Georgia's southern border with Florida. Cairo is the county seat and the largest city, and Cairo and Whigham are the only incorporated cities. Every parcel appears on one county digest, and a city can add its own levy, so read each line of the bill before you agree on a price.

The county had 26,236 residents at the 2020 census, and the July 2025 estimate of 26,590 is a 1.4% increase. About 21.2% of residents are 65 or older, which makes age-based exemptions relevant for many owners planning a move. Only 55 building permits were issued in 2025, so resale houses make up most of the market.

A midpoint tells you little about one parcel. Rely on the value printed on your own assessment notice, and ask the commissioner for a payoff number before you decide how to sell if taxes are behind.

sections.h2: Which Grady County offices handle valuation and billing?
sections.html:
Two offices divide the work. The tax commissioner's side bills land, buildings, business property, vehicles, mobile homes and timber. The Tax Assessor office, headed by a chief appraiser, deals with returns, values and conservation or agricultural applications.

  • Tax commissioner: 114 1st Street NE, Cairo, GA 39828, property phone 229-377-3322, open Monday to Thursday from half past seven in the morning until six in the evening and closed Fridays.
  • Tax commissioner and assessor service pages: 33 17th Avenue NW, Cairo, GA 39827, with eight-to-five weekday hours.
  • Parcel lookup: the commissioner's qPublic site has a search tool covering each parcel.

Call 229-377-3322 before you go, to confirm where to pay and the current hours. Updates appear on the county's commissioner page and assessor page.

The taxable base is 40% of fair market value as of January 1, and each yearly notice prints both figures. To challenge it, mail a letter to the Board of Tax Assessors with a postmark no later than 45 days after the notice was mailed. You pick the route on state form PT-311A: the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator.

A revaluation can delay notices and push appeal deadlines later in the year, so read the dates printed on your own notice rather than last year's calendar. Keep the notice and any appeal letter with your closing papers, because the title company may want to know which value the bill is built on.

The statewide default deadline is December 20, but Grady officials may choose December 1 or November 15, or split the bill into installments. Whatever your bill prints is the date that counts. No interest runs for 60 days after the bill is postmarked, and penalties can be added to balances left unpaid.

For an overdue parcel, get penalty and interest figures from the commissioner. Three other fixed points apply here:

  • A return for property you held on January 1 is accepted from January 1 until April 1.
  • Mobile homes sitting in the county on January 1 must be returned for tax by April 1, at the same time as the location permit.
  • Anyone seeking a refund of wrongly assessed tax has three years from payment to start the claim.

You can file a homestead application at any point after you move in, and April 1 is the final day for the first year. A missed filing counts as a waiver under state rules. The standard state deduction is $2,000 off assessed value. Ask the assessor whether any local amounts apply on top of it.

In early 2025 the county commissioners announced plans to opt out of the statewide adjusted base year homestead exemption. Ask the assessor what that means for your home before you tell a buyer the value is frozen.

  • Conservation use or preferential agricultural assessment: applications are accepted January 1 through April 1.
  • Freeport exemption on commercial and industrial inventory: available only where local voters adopted it, with filing on the return schedule.
  • A buyer files separately, since an exemption does not pass with the deed.

A November 2026 county notice shows a tentative millage rate that raises property taxes by 4.72 percent. The tentative rate is 12.64 mills, up .57 mill from 12.070 mills, the most the county could set without the increase. The notice gave hearing dates at 33 17th Avenue NW in Cairo.

That figure covers only the county's own levy. School and city rates come separately, and the final numbers show on your bill. Ask the commissioner's office for the rates that apply to your parcel when you need a payoff figure.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html:
Sellers move faster when the paperwork is ready. Pull together the last tax bill, the assessment notice with its mailing date, and any appeal letter you sent. If you applied for conservation use or an agricultural assessment, bring that application too, since a buyer will want to know whether the land stays in the program.

Then call the commissioner at 229-377-3322 and ask for the balance on the current year and any earlier years. A parcel with a recorded execution will not close until it is satisfied, and cities such as Cairo and Whigham may bill separately, so ask each office what is owed. With 66.1% of housing owner-occupied and few new builds, a clean tax record helps your house stand out among resale listings.

sections.h2: Handling the tax bill at closing
sections.html:
Whoever owns the parcel on January 1 is liable for that whole year. A January 2 sale changes nothing, and the state refunds no portion of the bill. Buyers and sellers divide it in the contract, and the settlement statement should state who pays what.

  • Find out from the commissioner what the parcel owes for the present year and earlier ones.
  • Alert the closing agent to any open appeal, since a revised bill may follow.
  • Pass the payoff figure and the receiving office to the closing agent.
  • Tell the office once a homestead exemption stops applying because you have left.

A cash buyer taking the house as-is still receives the parcel along with its tax history, so list any back taxes on the settlement statement. If a bill is unpaid, the payoff comes out of your sale proceeds at the table, which is easier to plan for when you have the figure in writing ahead of time.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Grady County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the tax commissioner's office in Cairo. One page gives 114 1st Street NE with Monday to Thursday hours, and the county service page gives 33 17th Avenue NW with weekday hours of eight to five. Call 229-377-3322 first to learn which counter takes payment.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Grady County value?
faqs.a: 45 days from the mailing date. Postmark your letter inside that period, address it to the Board of Tax Assessors on state form PT-311A, and name your route.

faqs.q: Does Grady County offer its own homestead exemptions?
faqs.a: The state's standard $2,000 exemption applies. Because of the county's 2025 plan to opt out of the base year freeze, ask the assessor which rules cover your home now.

faqs.q: If I close a Grady County sale in March, who owes that year's tax?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner. No part of the year is refunded, so the contract and settlement statement set the split, and the commissioner can confirm the amount before you close.

faqs.q: Is a refund possible for Grady County tax paid in error?
faqs.a: Yes, if the tax was erroneously or illegally assessed and collected. Ask in writing within three years of paying. When the assessment is under appeal, the refund follows once the final taxable value is fixed.
